poems:
9:00 p.m. The news gives way
to somebody's cooking competition.

9:01. The garage door opens for the last arrival,
the house's one drawbridge.

Four thumbs, one couch, no conversation.
Everything is being said.
A cat asleep on the warm router.

The bar has reached the volume where nobody hears the music.
The music is doing fine.

Tonight's pile:
six mismatched socks
one jersey, still damp
the good sheets
a napkin, by accident
something of the dog's

9:06. The show is paused on somebody's frozen face
for a debate about who that actor is.

9:07. The unfinished list is not going anywhere.
Neither are you.
Ice cracking in a glass, next room.

The teenager has emerged for food
and will now return to the cave
with a bowl of cereal the size of a hubcap.

9:10. A wet head on a dry pillow,
the day rinsed off it.

Somewhere a phone buzzes on a nightstand
and nobody picks it up.

9:12. Hand lotion, wrists last.
The day officially over at the skin.

The dog has decided it is bedtime
and is standing in the doorway about it.
At 9:14 the group chat regains consciousness.

The counter gets wiped a second time
by someone who believes they are the first.

Practice ran late. The car smells like a gym bag
and nobody says anything, out of respect.

To fold a fitted sheet:
corners inside corners.
Or do what everyone does,
roll it into a shape,
and shut the door.
The second glass of wine is poured with less ceremony than the first.

Homework at the table.
A pencil, a phone face-down,
the phone winning.
9:20. Nobody has started the thing they said they would start after dinner.

9:21. The movie theater lets out its early show,
everyone blinking like the deceived.

9:22. A car slows, isn't them,
keeps going.

9:23. Somebody just got a text that will change the week.
They are in line at a gas station.
The dryer buzzes. Everybody hears it. Nobody moves.
Two people, one blanket, an unresolved negotiation.
A basketball in the grass beside a driveway.

9:27. The taco truck's generator
feeds a line of four.

Someone is on hold with an airline
and has heard this saxophone before.
"No, I'm literally leaving right now, I'm literally in the car."

9:30. The list from this morning is being forgiven,
item by item,
by nobody in particular.

9:31. Someone is deciding about popcorn.
This is the largest decision left.

9:32. A towel over a door,
drying into a fossil of itself.

The show is on, the laundry is folded,
and two of the three in the room are on their phones.
The third has surrendered.
A skateboard clatters and stops. Clatters and stops.

Laugh track through a wall.
The wall unmoved.
The last of the coffee from this morning, cold, still in the mug on the desk.
Nobody in this house will admit to eating the last of it.

9:38. The drive-through speaker asks a question
made entirely of static.

Two hemispheres, one hour.
Somebody here is folding towels.
Somebody there is buttering toast before work.

You have been meaning to answer that message since Tuesday.
It can hold.

The teenager's door closes with the sound of a door closing
politely enough to count.

9:42. A car alarm chirps twice:
locked, loved.

9:43. Upstairs, the shower of somebody
with an early flight.

9:44. Inside, the bar is loud.
Outside, two people are having the real conversation
next to a dumpster.

9:45 p.m. Energy arrives with nowhere to go
and starts opening cabinets.
The kid who was not tired is asleep on the floor with shoes on.
A citronella candle, four adults, no decision.

The pharmacy is closed. The taqueria is not.
This is the correct arrangement.
You could start the book. The book has been patient.
Two bikes on a lawn, one upright.

Someone is being called for the second time.
The middle name is deployed.

9:52. Somebody's night is just starting:
eyeliner, confidence, a playlist doing pushups.

9:53. The freezer opened, surveyed,
closed without incident.

In the driveway, a car with the engine off and the radio on,
one song from home.

Somebody just said never mind
and meant a great deal by it.
Two shoes by the door, toes touching.

9:57. Tomorrow's clothes over the chair,
a small flag of intention.

9:58. The last bus on the outer route pulls out
with four people on it,
all of them different distances from home.
One more scroll and then bed, which is what was said at 9:20.
